$comment: Contract-coverage ratchet. unreviewedAccessibility and unknownCapabilities may only go DOWN; auditedComponents may only go UP. `node scripts/check/component-contract.mjs` fails if the library regresses past them — an unreviewed accessibility pattern or an unknown capability that was previously resolved. Reseed with --update after genuinely reducing a count.
$auditedComponents: Was 78. Re-based to 17 when `check:a11y` started requiring a named test behind every `pass`/`partial` (A11Y-001): 100 of the 508 dimension claims had nothing asserting them, and 62 components lost at least one. Nothing was un-audited — the number was never earned. It is now a floor over evidence rather than over assertions, and the per-slug/per-dimension detail is locked in scripts/config/a11y-audit-snapshot.json, which is the check that actually bites. Raise this as dimensions gain tests. Raised to 18 on 2026-08-22: `tree-view` gained `rtl` evidence (a direction-aware keyboard test using DirectionProvider), which was its last `not-audited` dimension. `audit` is computed, so a component only counts once every dimension is non-`not-audited` — 20 new dimension claims across 12 components moved the backed-evidence total 414 -> 434 while moving this figure by one, which is the ratchet behaving correctly rather than a disappointing result.
$unknownCapabilities: Was 0, then 119, now 4. The 0 was not a clean sheet: 125 of 145 families were reported `not-applicable` for density by derivation, which asserted a design decision — "this would look no different at any density and never should" — that nobody had made, and since this ratchet counts only `unknown`, the backlog was invisible. Correcting the derivation's fallback to `unknown` made it 119, which was honest and useless. All 119 have now been reviewed one at a time (DENSITY-001): 78 `unsupported` (they hardcode a metric density should govern), 33 `not-applicable` (content-intrinsic, author-sized, pass-through, or absent from layout), 4 `supported` (a thin wrapper around a control that already resolves the metric), and 4 left `unknown` — checkbox, radio-group, switch and rating, whose only density-relevant metric is a fixed hit target that compact would push below the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum. That is a design ruling, not a source fact. The per-slug values and the evidence for each are in scripts/config/density-applicability.json, which is the check that actually bites; this number is the aggregate and may only fall.
